Bhaiya's Teachings — Knowledge Base (Session 29)
Topic: Jap vs. Dhyan, Grahan Shakti, Temple Pretas, and Why Every Astral Body Gets "Activated"

Sour ce: A live Ashaeiynn sangat satsang (video transcript, ~1 hour 19 minutes) — a genuine back-and-forth session with extensive live audience participation, multiple named sangat members asking questions (Sheetal, V ipin, Jagpal Kaur , Rajni, Anshu, and others), and live Q&A, not a solo training monologue. Purpose: Chatbot knowledge — English version. Note on conversational content: this session contains substantial live sangat interaction — see the separate Hinglish conversational supplement (Part III) for curated exchanges.
1. OPENING LOGISTICS: THREE THINGS TO DO RIGHT NOW

This session opens with practical guidance for all Ashaeiynn members: for now , there ar e three things to do — complete all the training videos, begin your own jap (mantra chanting) practice, and stay in contact with your mentor , checking in at least every 15 days. Nearly every question that comes to a practitioner's mind — how to do jap, how long drishti takes to open, what negativity and pitrus actually ar e, how tantra-mantra-yantra works, and how to pr operly view things once drishti opens — has alr eady been answer ed somewher e acr oss the existing training videos. For any r emaining doubt after watching all videos and mentor sessions, practitioners can personally contact Bhaiya between 2:00 PM and 6:00 PM daily — while he may occasionally ask for a short delay if busy , he will always make time to talk. However , this teaching notes that r oughly 99 out of 100 typical questions ar e alr eady cover ed in the videos, so watching them first (rather than immediately seeking a personal call) is str ongly encouraged, since answering the same 99 questions individually for every practitioner is genuinely unworkable at scale.
2. JAP VS. DHYAN (MEDITATION): THE HIERARCHY AND WHY JAP COMES FIRST

In response to a sangat member's question about the differ ence between jap (chanting) and meditation, this teaching lays out a hierar chy: jap is the smallest/simplest practice, followed by dhyan (meditation), then dharana, then samadhi — each subsequent stage is pr ogr essively larger and deeper than the one befor e it. Jap is comparatively far easier and mor e accessible than meditation, which operates at a much larger level.
3. HOW REPEATED SOUND GENERATES ENERGY, EVEN WITHOUT MEANING

This teaching illustrates the underlying mechanism with a simple experiment: r epeating even a meaningless word (the example given is r epeating "bottle" continuously for half an hour) genuinely generates energy , because the practitioner's own sound energy is being converted into another form. Viewed through drishti, such meaningless repetition would appear as a "dark/black" energy — every specific repeated sound or name has its own ener gy source, color , and ef fect, meaning what you repeat matters, not just the act of repetition itself.
4. WHAT MAKES A MANTRA "SIDDHA" (ACCOMPLISHED): DIRECTED ENERGY, NOT JUST REPETITION

This teaching draws a sharp distinction between simply chanting any mantra and chanting a genuinely "siddha" mantra given by a guru. A siddha mantra alr eady has a "portal" established, and — critically — the energy it generates has alr eady been given an explicit dir ection, rather than being left to cir culate fr eely and uncontr olled. At Ashaeiynn, practitioners ar e taught to dir ect their jap-generated energy specifically to Hanuman Ji Maharaj's feet, with the practice of a specific subtle body (r eferred to in this teaching as "Parikshit bhai's" subtle body , described as functioning in a boon-granted capacity) tasked with actually delivering that energy onward. This produces a genuine exchange of energy: the practitioner's jap-energy travels toward Hanuman Ji Maharaj's r ealm, and in r eturn, a different energy — accompanied by the deity's own tattva (element) and doots (messengers) — comes back to the practitioner , since ener gy can neither be created nor destroyed, only exchanged.
5. WHY UNDIRECTED DHYAN (MEDITATION) IS ACTUALLY RISKIER THAN JAP

Meditation genuinely generates far mor e energy than simple jap — as the mind becomes still and aligned during meditation, a distinct ener gy forms and becomes visible outside the practitioner's body . However , this teaching str esses a serious risk: unlike jap-generated energy (which is deliberately dir ected), meditation-generated energy is not given any direction and simply cir culates fr eely ar ound the practitioner . Because an ordinary practitioner lacks drishti, they have no way of knowing that surr ounding bhoot-pr et (ghosts/spirits) can see this loose, undir ected energy and simply "snatch" it away — this is of fered as the explanation for why some sincere, dedicated meditators feel utterly drained and exhausted after long meditation sessions, having unknowingly had their generated ener gy taken from them by unseen entities.
6. WHY ASHAEIYNN TEACHES ONLY JAP AT FIRST, RESERVING DEEPER MEDITATION FOR LATER

Because of this risk, this teaching explicitly r ecommends that practitioners focus pur ely on jap for now , rather than pursuing open-ended, unsupervised meditation — protection/security requires real resources to establish, and only practitioners whose third eye (drishti) has genuinely opened are taught the "second stage" of meditation, to be followed later by a third stage, and eventually a path toward samadhi. Many sangat members present have already privately crossed the second and third stages of this progression, even if they don't openly mention it — this teaching credits this quiet patience and endurance specifically to genuine devotion (bhakti).**
7. WHY IDENTICAL PROTECTIVE RITUALS DON'T PROTECT EVERYONE EQUALLY

In response to a question about pr otective kavach (shielding), bandhan (binding), and nyasa (ritual invocation) practices performed befor e sadhna: this teaching confirms these do pr ovide genuine pr otection, but the AMOUNT of protection varies significantly fr om person to person, even when the exact same mantra, ritual timing, and water/materials ar e used identically .
8. GRAHAN SHAKTI ("RECEIVING CAP ACITY"): THE REAL DIFFERENCE BETWEEN TWO PRACTITIONERS

This teaching intr oduces the concept of "grahan shakti" (r eceiving/pulling capacity , roughly equivalent to "dimension" in English) as the actual explanation for why identical practices pr oduce differ ent protection levels. Grahan shakti refers to how much energy a person can pull into their body thr ough a given mantra, and how much of that energy they can genuinely stor e. A concr ete illustration is given: two practitioners perform the exact same pr otective kavach. A negativity (given the example name "Pawan Kumar") notices both practitioners generating energy thr ough Hanuman Chalisa r ecitation and attempts to attack both. Against a practitioner with strong grahan shakti (the example given is "V ipin bhai"), the kavach fully holds and the negativity cannot br eak thr ough. Against a practitioner with weaker grahan shakti, however , the same kavach can be torn thr ough, some energy drained, and the practitioner left feeling inexplicably "beaten up" and exhausted after their own puja — a pattern this teaching says many sincere practitioners have likely experienced without understanding why .
9. NOT ALL PRETAS ARE WEAK — SOME ARE THEMSELVES POWERFUL, DEVOTED SPIRITS

This teaching cautions against assuming that any pr eta will automatically flee fr om a simple mantra or Hanuman Ji Maharaj's name. Some pr etas wer e themselves genuinely devoted practitioners in life (having performed substantial worship and even r eceived bhog/offerings in multiple places befor e death), and carry r eal accumulated power/dimension into their post-death state — such pr etas ar e not intimidated by ordinary devotional r ecitation, and may even r espond in kind, since they too may be devotees of the very same deity being invoked.
10. WHAT ACTUALLY DISTINGUISHES A PRACTITIONER FROM SUCH A POWERFUL PRETA

When facing a pr eta who is itself a genuine devotee of the same deity , this teaching frames the r eal distinguishing factor as simply: who is the gr eater devotee, the living practitioner or the preta? This teaching notes bluntly that if a practitioner's own body/shell wer e removed, the practitioner themselves would simply be another preta — the underlying spiritual attainment, not the physical body , is what actually matters.
1 1. WHAT A PRETA ACTUALLY LOOKS LIKE, AND WHY DRISHTI IS RARELY SHARED

This teaching states that a pr eta, viewed thr ough drishti, is made of "thr ee elements" (teen tattva) and has a specific, recognizable appearance — something an ordinary person without drishti simply cannot per ceive. Three main r easons ar e given for why drishti (and this knowledge) is rar ely opened or shar ed widely: (1) people who alr eady have drishti often don't want others to discover that the "godly" help they claim to channel is actually assistance fr om pr etas rather than genuine devtas; (2) if a person's own drishti opened, they might see their own deceased family pitrus behaving inappr opriately within their own household, including toward the women in the family; and (3) opening drishti br eaks the "monopoly" that surr ounding pitrus and pr etas curr ently hold over a person, since the person could then dir ectly confr ont and dismiss them.
12. WHY DRISHTI RARELY OPENS IN HOUSEHOLDS THAT OFFER BHOG TO PITRUS

This teaching states a specific, memorable rule: in any household wher e pitrus ar e given bhog (ritual food offerings), not a single family member's drishti will open. Such households may still experience "sawari" (a pitru "riding"/possessing a family member during rituals), but genuine drishti will not be granted ther e — this teaching calls it a real irony that a person can carry the capacity for drishti within their own body and yet never open or use it, remaining trapped by this specific form of "blindness."
13. PRET AS CAN GENUINELY HELP SOMETIMES

This teaching acknowledges that some pr etas do genuinely help people (citing an example r eferred to as "Pr eetam"), without needing to change their fundamental spiritual state (yoni) to do so — echoing the earlier teaching that a spirit can simply have "a good heart."
14. EVEN GENUINEL Y POWERFUL ("PRAN-PRATISHTHIT") TEMPLES ARE SURROUNDED BY THOUSANDS OF PRETAS

This teaching states that temples which ar e genuinely "pran-pratishthit" (pr operly consecrated, with r eal established shakti) always have both a r eal energy sour ce AND thousands of pr etas gather ed ar ound them. The explanation given: when people die, many instinctively try to go dir ectly to a temple, believing they will meet God ther e — this produces dense, ongoing gatherings of pretas at popular temples and dhams, especially at lar ger or abandoned shrines that no longer have a living human channel properly directing their underlying shakti.
15. HOW UNSCRUPULOUS LOCAL TANTRIKS EXPLOIT THIS PRETA CONCENTRATION

This teaching describes how some tantriks specifically dir ect these gather ed pretas to fetch energy or perform tasks on their behalf via occult techniques. A small-time, "corner" tantrik will typically open his own drishti first, specifically because he needs it to dir ect pretas effectively — such a person can then create a problem for an ordinary person (via a preta) and later present himself as the very solution to that same problem, prompting repeated, dependent visits from someone who has no way of perceiving what is actually happening to them.
16. WHY THIS RELATES TO "KNOWING THE RULES OF THE GAME"

This teaching frames the entir e discussion ar ound a practical principle: if you know the actual rules of how the (astral) world works, you can change the game, and you can win it too — rather than remaining a vulnerable, uninformed participant.
17. WHY EVERY INDIAN'S ASTRAL BODY GETS ACTIVATED SO EARLY

This teaching identifies a specific vulnerability common to Indians: nearly everyone's sukshma (astral) body becomes active very early in life, typically thr ough infancy rituals — a grandmother , aunt, or other relative taking a newborn to a temple for naamkaran (naming) or blessing, wher e the baby's for ehead touches the gr ound (matth tekna) in devotion. This single act is often enough to activate that person's astral body for the rest of their life — a genuinely powerful entity or established deva shakti already active at that location does the activating.
18. WHAT "ASTRAL BODY ACTIVATION" ACTUALLY MEANS

Once a person's astral body is activated, they ar e described as having enter ed the "astral world" — becoming visible and r eachable to every kind of subtle-world entity active ther e: bhoot, pr et, pishach, kinnar , betaal, lakini, yakini, shakini, yatak, tantrik-mantrik-yantrik practitioners, and devi-devtas alike. Any of these can either attack a person or bless them, precisely because that person's astral body is switched on — this teaching describes it as one's spiritual "GPS" becoming active, meaning that from that point forward, simply knowing a person's name is enough for someone with the right knowledge to af fect them from a distance.
19. THIS IS NOT UNIQUELY AN INDIAN PHENOMENON

While this teaching notes having observed this pattern especially closely in India, it states that occult practice (tantramantra-yantra-based work) is also very common in the United Arab Emirates, and in several countries that make up the United Kingdom — describing these regions as having their own distinct methods, and noting this is a widespread, not uniquely Indian, phenomenon.
20. THE SOLUTION: CONNECT DIRECTLY WITH THE ASTRAL WORLD'S "MASTERS"

Since one's astral body cannot be un-activated, this teaching's r ecommended solution is to identify and dir ectly connect with the genuine "masters" of the astral world — such as Hanuman Ji Maharaj, Bhagwan Ram, or Bholenath — rather than r emaining vulnerable to whatever lesser entities happen to be nearby . These masters ar e described as always willing to help ("they give too") when appr oached pr operly .
21. GRAHAN SHAKTI DETERMINES HOW MUCH BLESSING YOU CAN ACTUALLY RECEIVE

This teaching illustrates the concept of grahan shakti with a container analogy: if a person appr oaches a devta with only a small bowl (katora), that is all they can r eceive and carry away , regardless of how gener ously the devta gives; a person with a bottle r eceives mor e; a person with a jug or tanker receives even mor e still. Devtas ar e described as never discriminating and always giving gener ously to everyone who asks — but a person's own grahan shakti (their "container size") is what actually limits how much of that fr eely-offer ed blessing they can genuinely r eceive and hold. This teaching states plainly: grahan shakti is dir ectly pr oportional to a person's dimension — the two concepts are essentially describing the same underlying capacity .
22. ASHAEIYNN'S STEP-BY-STEP PROCESS FOR SAFELY OPENING DRISHTI

This teaching outlines Ashaeiynn's own practical pr ocess: after aura-checking identifies any negativity , preta obstruction, tantra-mantra-yantra bondage, or similar issues in a practitioner's body , all of this is clear ed out and specifically sent to "Kalyan Lok" (a r ealm r eferenced in a separate training video). As this clearing happens, the practitioner is simultaneously started on mantra jap, so that the newly-clear ed space in the body doesn't r emain empty (since something will otherwise inevitably occupy any vacant space) — instead, that space progr essively fills with the mantra itself. This process continues until "Ram" is seated in every por e (rom-r om) of the practitioner's body , at which point no pr eta has the audacity to enter , since the body is alr eady saturated with jap. After the body is filled with mantra, work begins on the practitioner's chakras and overall dimension — this teaching clarifies that the seven chakras ar en't literally opened one at a time in strict isolation; rather , dimension is expanded broadly fr om the very first "chakra" stage onward, with the chakra names used mainly as convenient labels for describing the pr ocess. By r oughly the sixth chakra stage, a practitioner enters what this teaching calls the "third eye

session," and once drishti genuinely opens with Hanuman Ji Maharaj's pr otective shakti alr eady established behind the practitioner , whatever is subsequently seen cannot attack or mislead them — unlike drishti forced open through tantramantra-yantra methods, which this teaching describes as far more dangerous and prone to consuming the very practitioner who opened it that way .
23. ASHAEIYNN'S STATED LONG-TERM GOAL

This teaching states Ashaeiynn's explicit long-term goal: to give practitioners enough genuine astral-world knowledge that they can eventually r esolve pr oblems for their own families and futur e generations entir ely by themselves — potentially reaching the same level of capability as recognized contemporary figures known for such feats, achieved independently and through one's own understanding rather than dependency on any single teacher .

Part II — Q&A Pairs (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Q&A Pairs (Session 29, English)
Jap vs. Dhyan, Grahan Shakti, Temple Pretas, and Why Every Astral Body Gets "Activated"
User-style questions with answers gr ounded in this Ashaeiynn Foundation live satsang session. Gr eeting style: "Jai Siya Ram."

Q1. I'm new her e — what should I actually be doing right now? A: Jai Siya Ram! For now , focus on three things: complete all the training videos, begin your own jap (mantra chanting) practice, and stay in regular contact with your mentor , checking in at least every 15 days. Almost every question that comes to mind has already been answered somewhere in the existing videos.

Q2. Can I just call Bhaiya dir ectly whenever I have a doubt? A: Yes, between 2:00 PM and 6:00 PM daily , and he will always make time to talk, even if occasionally asking for a short delay if busy . That said, roughly 99 out of 100 typical questions are already covered in the training videos, so watching those first is strongly encouraged before requesting a personal call.

Q3. What's actually the differ ence between doing jap (chanting) and meditating? A: This teaching lays out a hierarchy: jap is the smallest, simplest practice, followed by dhyan (meditation), then dharana, then samadhi, each progressively lar ger and deeper . Jap is comparatively far easier and more accessible than meditation.

Q4. Does r epeating any word or sound generate r eal energy , even if it's meaningless? A: Yes — this teaching illustrates it with an example: repeating even a meaningless word like "bottle" continuously for half an hour genuinely generates ener gy , since your own sound ener gy is being converted into another form. Through drishti, though, such meaningless repetition would appear as a "dark" or negative-looking ener gy .

Q5. What makes a mantra actually "siddha" (accomplished) rather than just words I'm r epeating? A: A siddha mantra already has an established "portal," and — crucially — its generated ener gy has already been given an explicit direction, rather than being left to circulate uncontrolled. Simple repetition without that established direction isn't the same as a genuinely accomplished mantra.

Q6. Where does the energy fr om my jap actually go at Ashaeiynn? A: It's directed specifically to Hanuman Ji Maharaj's feet, with a particular subtle body (acting in a boon-granted capacity) tasked with delivering it there. This produces a genuine ener gy exchange: your jap-ener gy goes out, and in return, a dif ferent ener gy comes back to you, carrying the deity's own tattva and doots (messengers).

Q7. Meditation feels like it should be "better" than jap — is that true? A: Meditation does generate significantly more ener gy than jap. But this teaching warns that meditation-generated ener gy is left undirected and simply circulates freely around you — and because you likely lack drishti, you have no way of knowing that surrounding entities can simply take that loose ener gy for themselves.

Q8. Why do I sometimes feel completely drained after meditating, instead of r efreshed? A: This teaching's explanation is that meditation generates a lar ge amount of ener gy that isn't given any specific direction, and unseen bhoot-pret can notice and simply "snatch" this ener gy away from you without your knowledge, since you lack drishti to see it happening.

Q9. Should I stop meditating altogether then? A: This teaching recommends focusing purely on jap for now , rather than pursuing open-ended, unsupervised meditation. Only practitioners whose drishti has genuinely opened are taught the "second stage" of meditation, followed later by further stages and eventually a path toward samadhi.

Q10. If I do the exact same pr otective ritual (kavach/bandhan) as someone else, will I be equally pr otected? A: Not necessarily — this teaching confirms that identical rituals can produce very dif ferent levels of actual protection, because of a factor called "grahan shakti" (receiving/pulling capacity , roughly equivalent to "dimension"), which varies significantly from person to person.

Q1 1. What exactly is "grahan shakti"? A: It refers to how much ener gy a person can pull into their body through a given mantra, and how much of that ener gy they can genuinely store and retain. It's described as directly proportional to a person's overall dimension.

Q12. Why do I sometimes feel "beaten up" or exhausted after doing puja or a pr otective ritual? A: This teaching explains this through weaker grahan shakti — a negativity attacking a practitioner with a weaker protective kavach can actually tear through it, drain some of the generated ener gy , and leave that person feeling inexplicably exhausted, even while someone else doing the exact same ritual with stronger grahan shakti remains fully protected.

Q13. Will simply chanting Hanuman Ji Maharaj's name always scar e off any pr eta? A: Not necessarily — this teaching cautions that some pretas were themselves genuinely devoted practitioners in life, having performed substantial worship (and even received bhog in multiple places) before death, and carry real accumulated power . Such a preta isn't intimidated by ordinary recitation and may even respond in kind, since it may be devoted to that same deity too.

Q14. If a pr eta is also a devotee of the same god I worship, what actually determines who "wins"? A: This teaching frames it simply as a matter of comparative devotion and spiritual attainment — who is the greater devotee, you or the preta — rather than which specific deity's name is being invoked. It notes bluntly that without your physical body , you yourself would simply be another preta.

Q15. What does a pr eta actually look like, and why haven't I ever seen one? A: This teaching describes a preta, viewed through drishti, as made of "three elements" with a specific, recognizable form. Most people never see this because those who do have drishti often keep it hidden (to avoid exposing that their claimed "divine" help is really preta assistance), because it would expose their own family pitrus behaving inappropriately , and because it would break the "monopoly" that surrounding entities currently hold over them.

Q16. My family r egularly offers bhog to our pitrus — could that affect anyone's drishti opening? A: Yes, according to this teaching's stated rule: in any household where pitrus are given bhog of ferings, no family member's drishti will ever open. Such households may still experience pitru "possession" during rituals, but never genuine drishti.

Q17. Can a pr eta or ghost ever genuinely help a living person? A: Yes — this teaching acknowledges that some pretas do genuinely help people without needing to change their underlying spiritual state, since a spirit can simply have "a good heart," much like the point made in an earlier session.

Q18. If a temple has r eal divine power , does that mean it's fr ee of pr etas? A: No — this teaching states that even genuinely powerful, properly-consecrated ("pran-pratishthit") temples are surrounded by thousands of pretas, because many people who die instinctively try to reach a temple, believing they will meet God there. This is especially pronounced at lar ger or abandoned shrines with no living human channel directing the underlying shakti.

Q19. How do some small-time local tantriks seem to know exactly what's wr ong with people and offer to fix it? A: This teaching describes how such tantriks often open their own drishti first, specifically to direct nearby pretas to perform tasks for them — sometimes creating a person's problem via a preta, and then presenting themselves as the very solution to it, exploiting the person's total inability to perceive what's actually happening to them.

Q20. Why does this all seem to happen so much in India specifically? A: This teaching clarifies it's not unique to India — nearly every Indian's astral body gets activated very early in life (typically through infancy temple rituals like naming ceremonies), but this teaching notes that occult practice is also very common in the UAE and in parts of the United Kingdom, each with its own distinct methods.

Q21. What does it actually mean for my "astral body" to be activated? A: It means you become visible and reachable to every kind of subtle-world entity — bhoot, pret, pishach, and others, as well as devi-devtas — any of whom can either attack you or bless you.

This teaching describes it as your spiritual "GPS" switching on, meaning that from that point on, simply knowing your name is enough for someone with the right knowledge to af fect you from a distance.

Q22. If my astral body is alr eady activated and I can't undo that, what should I actually do? A: This teaching's recommended solution is to connect directly with the genuine "masters" of the astral world — Hanuman Ji Maharaj, Bhagwan Ram, or Bholenath — rather than remaining exposed to whatever lesser entities happen to be nearby . These masters never discriminate and always give generously to whoever approaches them properly .

Q23. If devtas give gener ously and don't discriminate, why doesn't everyone r eceive the same blessings? A: Because how much of that freely-given blessing you can actually receive and retain depends on your own grahan shakti — like the dif ference between approaching a devta with a small bowl versus a bottle, a jug, or a tanker . The devta gives fully either way , but your own "container size" limits what you can actually take away and keep.

Q24. What is Ashaeiynn's actual step-by-step pr ocess for safely opening someone's drishti? A: First, aura-checking identifies negativity , preta obstruction, or tantric bondage, which is cleared and sent to "Kalyan Lok." The practitioner is simultaneously started on mantra jap so the newly-cleared space fills with mantra rather than staying empty . This continues until the mantra is seated in every pore of the body , after which work begins on expanding overall dimension (labeled by chakra stage), eventually leading to a protected "third eye session" and a genuinely safe drishti opening.
